description.en: Eight memorial stops connecting the Bicol martyrs, local heroes and civic remembrance.

narration.en: The Oragon Monument stands in Plaza de Nueva Caceres near the river and market. Its sculptural groups depict Spanish arrivals and indigenous resistance. The city’s tourism account dates its unveiling to June 18, 2010, Naga’s 62nd cityhood anniversary.

sources.title: Naga City Tourism: Plaza de Nueva Caceres (Oragon Monument)

narration.en: José Rizal’s monument anchors the downtown park bearing his name. The city describes Plaza Rizal as a gathering place for debate and recreation. This stop celebrates that tribute without assigning an unestablished construction year.

The People Power Monument honors Corazon Aquino. A December 10, 2011 report records its unveiling during the previous day’s Batang Pinoy opening ceremonies at Plaza Quezon, attended by Jesse Robredo and Education Secretary Armin Luistro.

sources.title: The Philippine Star: Batang Pinoy national finals opening

narration.en: The Quince Martires marker distinguishes the fifteen martyrs’ fates: eleven executed at Luneta on January 4, 1897, two dead in prison and two in exile. The monument dates to 1926; its historical marker was unveiled in 1982.

sources.title: Philippine Registry of Cultural Property (NCCA): Naga City entries
Naga City Tourism: Plaza Quince Martires

narration.en: The old San Francisco belfry marks another chapter of the revolution. Its church marker identifies September 18, 1898 as the surrender of the last Spanish governor of Ambos Camarines to forces led by Elias Angeles and Felix Plazo.

sources.title: Philippine Registry of Cultural Property (NCCA): Naga City entries

narration.en: Jorge Barlin’s monument stands at Barlin and Arana streets. Born in Baao in 1850, he became the first Filipino consecrated as a Roman Catholic bishop on June 29, 1906. The plaza remembers his place in Philippine church history.

sources.title: Naga City Tourism: Plaza Jorge Barlin

narration.en: The school community raised this José María Panganiban memorial in 1930. In front of Naga Central School I’s Gabaldon building, his bust is accompanied by two schoolchildren: a tribute to the writer and propagandist’s patriotic example.

sources.title: Naga City Tourism: Jose Maria Panganiban Monument

narration.en: At Museo ni Jesse Robredo, a life-size bronze statue shows the former mayor seated on the ground in a shirt and shorts. Bicol Mail’s 2017 museum-opening report describes Jun Vicaldo’s design and the three pillars inscribed “Matino, Mahusay, Matapat.”

sources.title: Bicol Mail: NHCP chair and VP Leni to lead opening of Robredo museum
